title: AI-assisted sprite work in my iOS space idle game — The Little Restaurant
author: deedpool41
selftext:
I'm the developer of The Little Restaurant, a pixel-art space idle/clicker for iPhone and iPad.



I used generative AI for some visual assets. One shipped example is an eight-frame animation of a space cat looking at a painting, prepared as a transparent sprite sheet and integrated into the game. The sheet uses 96-by-96-pixel cells. The cat walks over, sits and looks at the painting, then returns to roaming. Fitting the animation to the existing character and scene was part of the asset workflow.



The attached video shows current gameplay. For other developers working with generated sprite sheets: how do you check character consistency and frame-to-frame stability before putting an animation into your game?



The Little Restaurant is free to download and supports English and Russian. Requires iOS/iPadOS 26 or later.
